summary.intent: Execute and ship GSD phase 68.1 (wiring the CipherBox web app onto the node/v3 read+write chain) end-to-end — run wave-based execution, close verification gaps through multiple rounds, then run the full ship-phase workflow (verify/secure/validate/simplify/SDK-E2E/CodeRabbit/PR/resolve-reviews), and finally triage new bugs found during live smoke-testing and plan the next phase (68.2) to fix an architectural read-chain duplication between the SDK and the web app.
summary.outcome: Phase 68.1 was executed across 33 plans and 3 verification rounds (e2e failures dropped from 202 to 2, both approved deferrals), shipped as PR #588 which merged to main with all CI green; a real production CAS-merge write-plane bug and several other defects were found and fixed during the ship pass; live smoke-testing then surfaced a shared-folder staleness bug and a file size/mtime display bug (fixed via a metadata mirror), which led to identifying a deeper architectural flaw (web duplicates the SDK's gated read chain) that was scoped and inserted as urgent Phase 68.2 (with Phase 69 extended for Rust-SDK parity) and committed to main.

repo: CipherBox v3 write-plane: WriteChildRef is keyed by node UUID (childId), never the ipnsName-based handle used by moveItem's caller-facing param — read plane (SealedChildRef) is keyed by ipnsName instead.

getWriteBodyParams fails open ({} / []) on a zero/absent writeKey by design (D-03) — but this means a transient IPNS resolve miss on an already-write-capable folder can seal an empty write-body, dropping the whole write chain (documented latent risk, not fixed).

CAS-merge (publishWithCas) must merge BOTH the read-body and write-body on a 409 conflict; decodeRemote previously never unsealed the remote write-body, so a losing writer's CAS retry would resealed the write-body from stale in-memory writeChildren, silently dropping the winner's WriteChildRef.
Terminal-owner zeroization rule (D-09): a callee must never zero a caller-owned buffer; a prior violation of this broke 48/89 E2E tests in an earlier phase.
createFolder in the v2→v3 cutover silently dropped the duplicate-name check that uploadFile still enforced — an inconsistent-contract regression found via CodeRabbit review.
CI's Test job does NOT run apps/web unit tests at all (web is covered only by Playwright web-e2e) — a broken test file (ipns.service.test.ts) can silently rot on main without ever going red in CI.
CodeRabbit CLI has a 150-file diff cap; when exceeded it silently skips the PR-level review — must be run directory-scoped locally (--dir apps/packages/tests) before shipping large phases.
Local dev API requires TEST_LOGIN_SECRET and DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL env overrides to match the e2e harness; never read .env files directly (permission denied) — override via env vars instead.

Email OTP dev-logging in EmailOtpService only fires when NODE_ENV is 'development' or unset; running the API under E2E env config (NODE_ENV=test/production) silently suppresses the OTP log with no error, and the OTP is otherwise unrecoverable (argon2-hashed in Redis).

mock-ipns-routing (tools/mock-ipns-routing) keeps IPNS records in an in-memory Map — every container restart wipes it; also its healthcheck used busybox `wget localhost` which resolves to ::1 while the app binds IPv4-only, causing a false 'unhealthy' status (fixed to 127.0.0.1 in docker-compose.yml).

V2 metadata schema (pre-node/v3) denormalized name+createdAt+modifiedAt into the parent's slim child pointer (FilePointer/FolderEntry) but resolved file size asynchronously from the file's own FileMetadata record — informing the decision to revert the interim size/mtime parent-mirror in favor of an SDK-owned resolved-listing cache.

The web app duplicates the SDK's read chain: apps/web/src/services/ipns.service.ts and file-metadata.service.ts reimplement resolve+anti-rollback-gate+unseal logic that also exists in packages/sdk, creating two sources of truth (SDK folderTree vs web's Zustand folder.store) and causing folder-state desync bugs (e.g., owner not seeing a collaborator's uploads until their own next write).

Web-side per-folder-open resolve of every child (via kind-cache.ts resolveKinds) already does the full IPNS-resolve+IPFS-fetch per child to read the plaintext `kind` field, discarding the sealed body — meaning adding size/mtime to that same pass costs an extra unseal (microseconds), not extra network, undermining the original justification for mirroring size into the parent metadata.

code.finding: decodeRemote/merge fixed to unseal and union writeChildren by childId on CAS 409 conflicts (previously only merged the read-body, silently dropping concurrent writers' WriteChildRefs).

moveItem never re-homed the moved child's WriteChildRef from source to dest write-body — fixed in 68.1-31 by unsealing under source writeKey, dropping from source, resealing under dest writeKey (keyed by resolved node UUID, not the ipnsName-based childId param).

navigateUp only re-derives the shared write key at share-root depth (isRootDepth gate) — navigating up/via-breadcrumb to a deeper subfolder restores it with a zero writeKey, breaking writes from that level until re-entering from the share root (deferred, documented known gap).

SealedChildRef was deliberately frozen to 5 fields (NODE-03 invariant); size/modifiedAt were added as optional additive mirror fields for display, then flagged for reversion once Phase 68.2 introduces an SDK-owned resolved-listing cache instead.
size and modifiedAt were hardcoded phase-63 stubs ('-' and formatDate(0)) because SealedChildRef never carried those fields — root cause of the Jan 1 1970 date / '-' size display bug.

workflow: For long-running background e2e suites, agents frequently 'lose the wake' (their completion notification never fires or their session gets evicted) — mitigate with an independent disk-based watchdog plus resuming via SendMessage while the transcript is still warm.
Always verify a commit landed via `git log -1` before retrying after a timeout — 1Password SSH commit signing produces frequent false-negative timeouts (exit 143) while the commit actually succeeds.

Never git stash in worktree-isolated executor agents — shared refs/stash across worktrees can revert another agent's in-progress work; caught twice this session via self-reported incidents, recovered via manual reapply.

When re-running a suite after fixes, always corroborate against a fresh full-run artifact rather than trusting individual spec re-runs — serial/describe.serial cascading aborts can mask whether earlier fixes actually hold under real execution order (found a spec-order race in full-workflow 3.9 this way).

GitHub review tooling requires a full re-sweep for new threads after each push — Greptile re-reviewed fix commits and raised additional findings across multiple rounds; must poll and resolve iteratively, not just once.

Rebuilding a package's dist (e.g., sdk-core) requires downstream consumers (sdk, then web/vite) to also rebuild/re-optimize before a smoke test reflects the new code — vite caches pre-bundled deps and needs a --force restart.

friction: Multiple background agents died mid-task on session/usage limits (Fable credit exhaustion, Claude session resets) requiring manual disk-state recovery and re-dispatch, costing significant orchestration overhead across the ship-phase pass.
CodeRabbit's 150-file cap silently skipped review both locally and on the PR itself, requiring directory-scoped local runs as a workaround.
Repeated 1Password commit-signing timeouts (exit 143) required verify-before-retry discipline to avoid duplicate/lost commits.
Full 208-spec Playwright suite runs took ~20 minutes each and were run many times (baseline, confirmation, per-fix re-runs, final closing run), making the ship+gap-closure cycle very slow.

Lost background-agent wake-ups occurred repeatedly (exit-gate agents parking after launching a long background suite and never getting notified), requiring watchdog scripts and manual SendMessage resumption.

OTP extraction for local smoke testing was blocked for an extended diagnostic chain because the API was running under E2E env config that silently suppressed dev-mode OTP logging with a 200 response and no visible error.
Wrong cwd (stuck in docker/ from an earlier cd) caused a false 'ROADMAP.md missing' scare mid-session.
open_items: Phase 68.2 (SDK-Owned Read Chain and Resolved Folder Listings) inserted into the roadmap — moves the gated resolve+anti-rollback+unseal logic and folder listing cache into the SDK, deletes web's duplicate read services (ipns.service, file-metadata.service, kind-cache, useFileSize), and reverts the interim size/mtime SealedChildRef mirror back to its frozen 5 fields.
Phase 69 (Rust SDK) scope extended to add read-chain-ownership parity for the FUSE/WinFsp layer, mirroring the 68.2 design.
